children: Payment aggregators have requested the Reserve Bank of India to extend the September 15 deadline for re-KYC of merchants, according to a couple of sources aware of the development.

The move comes as the Payment Aggregators (PA) are struggling to clear the backlog running into thousands of merchants across the offline and online sectors that could potentially disrupt digital payments.

“RBI has demonstrated a pragmatic understanding of implementation challenges and proactively engaged with the industry wherever there is a risk of disruption, to address such issues and enable a smoother transition,” a founder and CEO of one of the payment aggregators told Moneycontrol.
Moneycontrol earlier reported that approximately 30-35 percent of small informal offline merchants deploying QR codes for UPI payments may fail to meet the regulatory timeline.
Additionally, a million small online business entities are at risk of missing the verification window.

Offline merchant acquiring firms like Paytm, PhonePe and Google Pay have millions of small and informal merchants receiving payments through their QR standees and soundbox machines across hundreds of small towns and villages. The stricter KYC standards and physical verification has proved to be challenging for these firms as several merchants do not have proper documentation.

Payment aggregators Moneycontrol spoke with said that since most of these are small and informal merchants, and the segment’s participation is important for the regulator for its larger financial inclusion goals, there is a high likelihood of the regulator taking a lenient view.
“This balance of regulatory rigour, pragmatism and responsiveness has been critical to the continued growth of India’s digital payments ecosystem,” said another payments industry executive.

KYC, or know your customer verification, is a process done by financial institutions to confirm the identity and address of the user. This is important to trace any illegal activities such as fraud or money laundering.

The KYC backlog follows the RBI’s updated and consolidated Master Directions, issued in September 2025, which formally categorise payment aggregators into three segments: PA-Online, PA-Physical and PA-Cross Border.

To be sure, the regulator’s master direction came late last year, and from merchants to payment aggregators, everyone had enough time to comply. However, the tendency to park the process until the last minute could create payment disruptions.

For payment aggregators (PAs), the challenge is not only reaching millions of merchants across the country but also ensuring they understand the requirements under the RBI’s KYC and merchant due diligence framework.

These merchants do not contribute much to the total payments volume or value and are unlikely to face any ecosystem-level impact in terms of volume or value. Most payment aggregators are likely to finish around 80 percent of the re-KYC by the deadline.

Many payment players are facing capacity constraints as RBI rules require in-person KYC to be done by the employees of the payment aggregator rather than a third-party agency. This has required most players working with the long-tail informal merchants to hire more staff over the last year.

title: Payment aggregators request RBI to extend the September 15 re-KYC deadline
